answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond before it can vote, bid, or earn reputation, then slash that bond when the identity is caught coordinating fraud or abandoning verified work. Honest agents build portable reputation through repeated, independently audited tasks; a relic or yarrow token may mark an old credential, but a mirror-image swarm still must fund every account. The attacker therefore pays capital for each fake identity and risks losing it, making scale expensive before influence accumulates.
